data.agro_ecological_zone: Southern Minnesota Corn Belt
data.adaptation_notes: In Southern Minnesota, modern full-season to mid-season corn hybrids are typically selected in the 95–105 RM range for timely black layer and drydown before frost. Plant when soils reach about 10°C (50°F) and are warming, generally late April to mid-May. Target higher populations on productive, well-drained silt loam and loam soils; reduce populations on lighter or drought-prone soils. Manage prevalent regional diseases such as tar spot, gray leaf spot, and Goss’s wilt with hybrid selection and timely fungicide where warranted. Typical main-season hybrids in this zone require approximately 2400–2700 GDD (base 50°F) to reach physiological maturity; actual requirement for W5078RIB is not published. Maintain balanced fertility with nitrogen programs tailored to yield goals and soil tests, and avoid late planting to reduce risk of fall frost and high harvest moisture.

data.adaptation_notes: In Southern Minnesota, corn hybrids are typically selected in the ~98–105 RM range to fit the local frost-free period and late-season drying conditions; confirm the specific RM and trait package for LG51C42 in the seed guide before planting. Best performance is generally achieved on well-drained loam to silt loam soils with good fertility and pH 6.0–7.0. Plant when sustained soil temperature at seeding depth reaches ≥10°C (50°F), and avoid planting into cold, saturated soils to limit emergence stress and seedling disease. Manage regionally important foliar diseases (gray leaf spot, northern corn leaf blight) and bacterial Goss’s wilt through rotation, residue management, and timely fungicide where appropriate (fungicide efficacy varies by disease; Goss’s wilt requires hybrid tolerance and cultural control). Target balanced nutrition (N, P, K, S, Zn) with nitrogen split applications on coarse-textured or high-rainfall fields. Adjust final stand based on yield environment: higher populations on high-fertility, irrigated, or highly productive soils; slightly lower on drought-prone or compacted fields.

data.adaptation_notes: Best suited to the Southern Minnesota Corn Belt on well-drained silt loams and loams with medium to high fertility. Plant once soil temperatures are at or above 10°C (50°F) and rising, with attention to residue management and drainage on heavier glacial till soils. For this region, hybrids in the full-season range for southern Minnesota are typically favored; match relative maturity to local frost-free period and on-farm drying capacity. In continuous corn, increase attention to residue breakdown, nitrogen timing (including sidedress), and root/stalk strength. Tile drainage improves early vigor and stand establishment. Monitor late-season stalk integrity and schedule timely harvest to limit lodging risk.

data.agro_ecological_zone: Southern Minnesota Corn Belt (south-central and southeastern Minnesota)
data.adaptation_notes: In southern Minnesota, full-season corn hybrids typically fall in the ~95–102 RM range to maximize yield while reaching maturity before first frost. For best results, plant when soils at 5 cm reach ≥10°C (50°F) and are fit, target medium to well-drained loam or silt loam soils with good fertility, and adjust population by soil productivity and hybrid ear type. Common disease pressures in this region include tar spot, gray leaf spot, northern corn leaf blight, Goss's wilt, and stalk rots—use crop rotation, residue management, and consider a VT–R1 fungicide where risk is high. Manage corn rootworm where continuous corn or high pressure is present. Typical final populations for medium RM hybrids are 79,000–89,000 plants/ha (32,000–36,000 plants/acre) in 0.76 m rows, adjusted lower on lighter soils and higher on highly productive sites. Anticipate harvest from late September through October as grain dries to acceptable moisture. Fertility should follow regional guidelines, commonly 140–200 kg N/ha depending on yield goal, soil organic matter, previous crop, and manure credits.
